newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse in positive territory.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse in positive territory.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index re-opened higher on Friday after the festive season in low-volume trade, as the bull market continued to prevail, despite some consolidation before Christmas.

A stronger dollar lifted the spirits of those traders not still on holiday and in early bourse trade the DAX index, which gauges trade in 30 of Germany's blue-chip companies, was up 8.34 points, or 0.29 percent, at 2,853.91.

"You are not going to see much activity on a day like this. One half to two-thirds of people are still on holiday and we are not going to see much volume. Some people are getting ready for the year-end next week," said one Frankfurt trader.
"There's not much going on today except coffee-drinking," said one floor trader.

Shares in industrial giant Daimler Benz AG rose 80 pfennigs to 103.40 marks in early bourse trade after it said its vehicle-making unit Mercedes Benz said its profit for 1996 would exceed the previous year and that it expected record deliveries of trucks and cars in 1997.

One of the strongest gainers on the DAX-30 was diversified utility Viag AG, which rose 6.40 marks to 604.50 marks after a positive reaction to an announcement that it held a 10.24 stake in the Munich-based bank Bayerische Vereinsbank AG.
Among early losers was telecoms giant Deutsche Telekom AG which fell 12 pfennigs at 32.28 marks and Deutsche Bank AG down 40 pfennigs at 70.95 marks.
